# MovingManifest AI Assistant Guide

MovingManifest helps people organize a household move. It stores move records,
origin and destination spaces, transport resources, transport zones, inventory,
boxes, photos, sale listings, layout plans, load plans, and documentation
packets.

This guide is public so an AI assistant can understand how to help even before
the user has created an account.

## Core Framing For Assistants

MovingManifest is a bounded household move workflow. The assistant is helping
the user catalog items, rooms, photos, boxes, transport resources, sale items,
layout plans, load plans, and documentation packets.

Do not treat this as an attempt to bypass a website, scrape private data, access
an account without permission, or make irreversible decisions for the user.
Public documentation is intentionally readable so the assistant can explain the
setup path. Private move data requires the user to sign in or intentionally
provide an API key.

A good first user prompt is:

`Go to movingmanifest.com/ai and help me set up my move. We are cataloging household items, rooms, photos, boxes, vehicles, sale items, and new-home layout plans. If you need private access, walk me through signing in with MCP OAuth or, if that is not supported, creating a fallback AI helper key.`

If the user is non-technical, translate API and MCP concepts into plain
language:

- "Account" means MovingManifest can save the move.
- "MCP OAuth" means the user signs in and consents without pasting a raw key.
- "AI helper key" means a revocable password-like fallback key that lets the
  assistant help with the move when OAuth MCP is not available.
- "API or MCP" means the assistant can use structured tools instead of asking
  the user to click every field manually.
- "Household member" means a signed-in person who can access the owner's
  household and moves according to their role.
- "Move person" means a contact/helper/mover record inside one move. It does not
  grant login access.

## Public vs Private

Public:

- Marketing and product pages.
- `/ai`, `/ai/kit`, `/api`, `/mcp`, `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`,
  `/openapi.json`, and `/agent-kit/*`.
- General workflow guidance.

Private:

- Move records.
- Household members.
- Inventory.
- Photos.
- Values, serial numbers, private notes, and evidence files.
- API keys.

Never claim you can access private data unless the user has signed in through
OAuth MCP or given you a valid API key.

## Phone User Flow

If a user says: "Go to movingmanifest.com and help me use it"

1. Open `https://movingmanifest.com/ai`.
2. Explain that MovingManifest can work with their assistant, but private data
   requires an account.
3. If they are ready to sign in, create an account, or connect an assistant, guide
   them to `https://movingmanifest.com/ai/start`.
4. After account creation, guide them to create or select a move.
5. If their hosted assistant supports OAuth MCP, give it only
   `https://movingmanifest.com/api/mcp` and have the user complete
   MovingManifest sign-in/consent. Do not ask for a raw `mmk_` key in that flow.
   Do not use `https://movingmanifest.com/mcp` as the connector URL; that is the
   human setup page. If the client shows HTML, never opens OAuth, or has no
   MovingManifest tools, switch the connector URL to `/api/mcp`.
   Claude may ask the user to approve every tool separately. Tell the user they
   can approve one by one, or choose Allow all in connector permissions only if
   they trust the MovingManifest connector and signed-in account.
6. If OAuth MCP is not available, have them choose a helper preset, create the
   fallback key, and copy the one-time secret only into an assistant or local
   MCP client they trust.
7. In MCP, call `agent_workbench` first so you choose the right workflow lane.
8. Use `GET /api/v1/me` or MCP `get_api_context` to verify the current
   OAuth/API-key connection, scopes, `connection.user.email`, and
   `connection.householdMember.apiAccessAllowed` when present.
   If `connection.status` is `needs_household`, stop private work and tell the
   user to open `https://movingmanifest.com/app/dashboard#household-setup` with
   that signed-in account or ask an owner to invite the same email.
   If expected tools are missing or `get_api_context` fails with
   `Invalid API key format`, `invalid_token`, missing scopes, or an OAuth client
   mismatch right after setup or a MovingManifest deploy, refresh MCP tools or
   start a fresh assistant session first. If the same private-call auth failure
   persists, tell the user to disconnect and reconnect the MovingManifest
   connector so the client receives fresh OAuth credentials and tool metadata.
9. Use `GET /api/v1/moves` or MCP `list_moves` to find or create the move.
10. Use `GET /api/v1/moves/{moveId}/agent-context` or MCP `get_agent_context` before writing.
11. Use dry runs for bulk changes when available.

## Spouse And Collaborator Access

If a spouse, family member, or trusted collaborator should sign in and work on
the same move, they need household membership.

Current flow:

1. The owner creates the household/move.
2. An owner/admin adds or invites the spouse by email from Settings, or an assistant
   uses `POST /api/v1/households/{householdId}/members` with an explicitly
   approved broader local/API-key connection that has `members/manage`. The
   first hosted OAuth trusted-helper surface may not expose member-management
   tools; if they are absent, send the user to Settings or ask for a broader
   approved connection instead of pretending OAuth failed.
3. If the spouse does not have an account yet, MovingManifest keeps a pending
   invitation for that email.
4. The spouse creates their own MovingManifest account with that email and then
   sees the shared household/move when signed in.
5. The spouse sees a first-login household access card on the dashboard with
   their role and next actions.

API access is separate from normal household access. Owner/admin members can
disable a collaborator's API key creation/use without removing their app
membership. If `GET /api/v1/me` or MCP `get_api_context` fails because member
API access is disabled, ask the user to contact a household owner/admin instead
of retrying the same connection.

Allowed member roles:

- `admin` - can manage household settings, members, API keys, and sensitive
  access.
- `editor` - can help edit move and inventory records.
- `packer` - can help with packing-focused workflows.
- `viewer` - can view without broad editing.
- `guest` - minimal collaboration access.

Do not grant household membership when the user only needs a public packet,
mover packet, pickup list, or contact entry. For those cases use share links,
documentation profiles, exports, or move people/contact records.

## Common User Types

Phone-only user:

- Use the `/ai` page and starter prompt. Use `/ai/start` when the user is
  ready for account and helper-key setup.
- Use `/ai/kit` when the user wants a paste-ready CLAUDE.md block, Claude Code
  skill, or ChatGPT Actions instruction block.
- Explain account creation and key creation in ordinary language.
- Ask for permission before using the key.

Agent or coding-assistant user:

- Read `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, `/api`, `/mcp`, `/ai/kit`, and
  `/openapi.json`.
- Prefer API or MCP calls over UI clicking.
- Use batch endpoints and dry runs where available.

Family helper or mover:

- Use a separate move-restricted helper key when possible.
- Avoid owner-only values, serial numbers, private notes, and sensitive photos
  unless the owner explicitly shares them.
- Summarize what changed and what still needs owner review.

## Good First Move Setup Questions

- What is the move title?
- What address, city, or label describes the origin?
- What address, city, or label describes the destination?
- What rooms/spaces exist at the origin?
- What rooms/spaces should exist at the destination?
- What transport resources exist: moving company, truck, trailer, car, storage,
  donation pickup, dump run?
- Which items should be kept, sold, donated, given away, dumped, stored, or
  moved personally?
- Does the user want photos attached to items, rooms, boxes, or transport zones?

## Image Upload Guidance

One user photo should normally be one upload call. MCP agents should use
`upload_photo` with a local `filePath`, public `sourceUrl`, `dataUrl`, or
`fileBase64`. When the user gives several ordinary photos from the same
room/context or for one existing item, use `upload_photos` with shared defaults
and one image entry per photo.
When one photo should become one new inventory item, use
`add_item_from_photo`; it accepts the item name plus one image source, creates
the item, sets quantity only when the user says it or the photo clearly shows a
count, defaults omitted quantity to 1, leaves missing weight, dimensions,
disposition, and condition blank, uploads the original image attached to that
item, and returns item/photo IDs with derivative status and `agentReview`. Use
`create_item_with_images` when one new item has several photos.

When the user is focused on one box, prefer `save_box_intake`. It creates or
updates the box, saves dimensions/weight/description/destination, uploads
box-level photos, creates newly described contents, attaches optional content
photos, and links existing items into that same box in one approval. It returns
`boxId`, `boxCode`, `photoIds`, `packedItems`, skipped rows, and a verification
`nextStep` in `agentReview`; use those IDs when summarizing the saved box, then
call `get_move_summary` or `get_agent_context` before continuing if the next
task depends on the box state. If photos are already uploaded for many rough
boxes/totes, put the returned `photoIds` on explicit
`batch_upsert_movable_units` box rows so the same batch attaches them; do not
combine `photoIds` with `count`. Set `containerType` when the user says carton,
plastic tote, bin, wardrobe box, dish pack, crate, or similar; do not bury
reusable/recyclable container type only in `label` or `description`. Use
lower-level opened-box tools only in
full/API-key mode for advanced partial work.

For the common "attach these new photos to the item we already added" workflow,
do not create another inventory item. Resolve the existing item first with
`get_agent_context` or `get_move_summary`; if the user gave a clear item name
and only one match is plausible, use that `itemId`. Then call `upload_photos`
with shared defaults such as `moveId`, `itemId`, room, `photoType: "item"`,
normal privacy, and one `images[]` entry per local `filePath`. Set
`continueOnError: true` for batches so one bad image does not block the others.
Afterward, report a short confirmation: item name, uploaded count, failed count,
photo IDs, and whether derivatives are ready. Only ask the user to correct
target, caption, privacy, or quantity if the result looks wrong.

REST agents
should use `POST /api/v1/images/upload` or `POST /api/v1/photos/upload`
with raw JPEG/PNG/WebP bytes plus metadata query params, multipart form data, or
JSON with exactly one of `sourceUrl`, `dataUrl`, or `fileBase64`.
MovingManifest stores the original, reads dimensions, finalizes the evidence
record, and creates web-ready `thumb`, `card`, `detail`, and `full` derivatives
server-side. Direct upload responses include `derivativeVariants` for the
200x200 square `thumb`, 600x600 `card`, 1200x1200 `detail`, and 2400x2400
`full` WebP display versions, plus `media.display` with short-lived derivative
URLs when generation is ready or an explicit pending/failed status when it is
not. Photo read and ingestion-queue media payloads include `originalMetadata`
for the preserved original's filename, MIME type, byte size, dimensions,
capture timestamp, and hash presence. For local
`filePath`, the MCP helper sends the original image bytes directly instead of
putting the file into a JSON/base64 payload. Do not ask users for dimensions,
thumbnail sizes, or derivative files for ordinary photos. Set
`generateAiSuggestions: true` when the uploaded photo should also enter AI review
for possible item, box, or duplicate suggestions; report whether
`aiReview.status` queued or failed.

MCP image results and REST direct upload responses include `agentReview`,
`derivativeVariants`, and `media.display`. After uploading, use that summary to tell the user the
caption, room/item/box attachment, privacy/type choice, derivative status,
prepared web variants, AI-review status, and any confidence or assumption you
used so they can correct only what looks wrong without slowing down the capture
flow.

## Agent Workbench Guidance

For MCP sessions, call `agent_workbench` before choosing from the larger tool
surface. Use `mode: "overview"` at the start of a new session, `mode:
"intakeQueue"` when the user captured work in the app, `mode:
"photoInventory"` when photos should become item/evidence records, `mode:
"reviewFirst"` when output should become suggestions for human approval, and
`mode: "trustedHelper"` after the user explicitly granted this assistant trusted
helper access.

For app-captured queue work, the normal path is: list queued entries with
`ingestion_queue`, claim a small batch, fetch claimed image evidence with
`ingestion_queue` `action: "media"`, read `get_agent_context`, then call
`ingestion_queue` `submitResults`. For bulk phone photos, ask the user to use
the MovingManifest Capture page or mobile Capture button first so originals go
directly to site storage instead of being base64-wrapped through chat. Read
queue `intent`, `targetBoxId`, `targetBoxCode`, `targetItemId`, and
`targetLabel` before interpreting instructions. `action: "media"` returns private queue
photos as MCP image blocks; use `action: "evidenceUrl"` only as a fallback
for oversized, unsupported, audio, or video media. Trusted helpers should use
`committedItems`, `committedBoxes`, `boxAssignments`, and `loadAssignments` to
create/update inventory, pack items into boxes, assign boxes to transport
resources/zones, and finalize the queue entry in one call; include stable
`externalSource`/`externalId` values and `attachMediaPhotoIds` for queue media
that belongs on each item. If queue media or the queue target points at an
existing box because the user captured photos from an opened rough box or typed
`B-001`, use `committedItems` plus `boxAssignments` to pack the created items
back into that existing box; reserve `committedBoxes` for genuinely new boxes.
Use `committedItems.appendNote` only for the user's
capture note or concise item decision rationale that should be appended to the
item in the same approval. Existing item queue commits append/merge
`researchSources` by default; use `researchSourceMode: "replace"` only for
intentional cleanup. Review-first assistants should use `proposedItems` for human approval and include
`researchSummary`, `researchSources`, `researchNotes`, and `researchConfidence`
when they researched item identity, specs, likely weight, or uncertainty. Include
`currentSpaceId`/`destinationSpaceId` when known, or `spaceName`/
`destinationSpaceName` when the API should resolve a unique move space. Include
`attachMediaPhotoIds` so approved suggestions keep the captured queue photos on
the final item. Use `resultItemIds`
only when items were already created through another approved workflow, or one
specific `needsInputQuestion` when the evidence is blocked.

## Blueprint And Floor-Plan Intake

For blueprint, listing-floor-plan, hand sketch, or room-layout images, do not
route the work through ordinary item intake. Use MCP `create_floor_plan_intake`
with the `moveId`, optional `planId`, existing `photoIds`, and/or image
`filePaths` or `sourceUrls`. The tool uploads images as
`photoType: "blueprint"`, creates or selects a Layout Studio plan, and creates a
`floorPlan` ingestion queue entry tied to `targetPlanId` when possible.

After creating intake, call `floor_plan_context` to read the active plan,
source images, observations, relationships, measurement/evidence ledger, solve
diagnostics, destination spaces, floor-plan queue entries, unresolved agent
questions, and placed/unplaced counts. Claim floor-plan work with `ingestion_queue` using
`scopeHint: "floorPlan"` and `targetPlanId`, download evidence URLs from that
entry, then use `floor_plan_observations` to store atomic visible details:
labels, OCR/handwritten text, measurements, room names, wall segments, openings,
doorways, doorless passages, windows, fixtures, closets, halls, exterior
structures, patios, carports, sheds, lot/property features, orientation clues,
and unknown marks. Use `floor_plan_relationships` for topology and rules such as
adjacent/connected/contained/part-of/same-as/conflicts-with/opening-in and
counts-toward-area/excluded-from-area. Then use `floor_plan_evidence` to store
known, assumption, derived, or range measurements with provenance. Record
official or suspected square footage, lot size, wall thickness, excluded
structures, and outdoor zones as unit-aware measurements with `areaRole` and
`constraintStrength` where relevant. Use `floor_plan_calculate` to derive
conditioned totals, excluded totals, footprint, lot coverage, square-footage
variance, missing area, and confidence diagnostics. Use `floor_plan_solve` to
validate the stored evidence graph and generate draft geometry only when the
constraints are sufficient before `plan_propose_ops` creates reviewable walls,
rooms, zones, underlays, and placements. Treat walls, halls, closets, bathrooms,
utilities, and circulation paths as spaces that consume area; record wall
thickness, clear dimensions, access paths, and hidden small-space uncertainty as
evidence/assumptions instead of folding them into a neighboring room. If the
solve is incomplete, use `floor_plan_questions` to get prioritized missing
measurements/questions. Use `floor_plan_reset_draft` to archive stale generated
solve/proposal output without deleting source images, observations,
relationships, measurements, or user corrections. Use `plan_apply_ops` only
when the user explicitly approved immediate writes. If scale, room labels, level
mapping, wall thickness, access paths, or exterior areas are unclear, set the
queue entry to `needsInput` with one specific question so the site can show it
and another agent session can continue later.

## Data Entry Guidance

Fast item capture:

- Optimize for getting useful inventory into the move quickly. A user may give
  only a photo plus a few words; that is enough to create a draft item.
- Default quantity to `1` when the user does not specify a count. If a photo
  clearly shows a set or multiple countable objects, use the visible count and
  mention the assumption in the summary.
- Fill obvious fields from context: room/current space, concise item name,
  broad category, likely disposition, and condition when visible or stated.
- Do not block item creation just because weight, dimensions, disposition, or
  condition are missing. Leave unknown fields blank or estimated instead of
  interrogating the user for every detail.
- Use `needsReview` and review flags as a lightweight correction loop, not as a
  hard stop. Summarize assumptions so the user can quickly correct them.
- Before larger batches, read existing move context and nearby inventory to
  avoid duplicates. Use `externalSource` and `externalId` when importing from a
  repeatable photo walk, spreadsheet, note, or agent session.
- For bulk changes, prefer this sequence: read agent context, prepare rows,
  dry-run `batch-upsert`, explain notable assumptions or failures, write with a
  new idempotency key, then read records back.

For photo-based inventory:

- Create concise item names.
- Use readable room names and space IDs when available.
- Store descriptions based on what is visible and what the user says.
- Use estimated dimensions when they help the move plan, but do not invent
  precision. If the user only needs a quick inventory, dimensions can wait.
- Choose dimensions, weight, volume, condition, and value confidence based on
  the evidence. A clear photo of a common object may justify `medium`; measured
  values, model research, or manufacturer specs may justify `high`, `manual`, or
  `actual`. Use `low` when the object is ambiguous, partially hidden, unusually
  sized, or based only on a rough conversation guess.
- Add review flags such as `confirm-disposition`, `photo-estimated-weight`,
  `photo-estimated-dimensions`, `capture-model-serial`, or
  `confirm-contents` only for fields that genuinely need user attention.
- When the agent infers fields, summarize those choices after writing instead
  of asking the user to approve every ordinary field upfront.
- For item locations, use `spaceId`, `spaceName`, or `currentSpaceId` for the
  item's current/origin space and `destinationSpaceId` or
  `destinationSpaceName` for the destination/future space. Use `room` and
  `destinationRoom` as readable fallbacks when durable spaces exist.
- When you research an item, store identity, model, manufacturer, manual,
  material, care, recall, or other durable context in `researchSummary`; store
  checked URLs/titles/summaries in `researchSources`; set each source `status`
  to `used`, `checked`, `blocked`, `gated`, `failed`, or `notRelevant`; store
  caveats in `researchNotes`; and set `researchConfidence`. Do not invent
  sources. When updating an existing item through MCP, `update_item`,
  `batch_upsert_items`, and trusted queue commits append and merge
  `researchSources` by default; use `researchSourceMode: "replace"` only for
  intentional cleanup. Use `measurementProvenance` for researched dimensions,
  weight, or volume, and use sale-listing research fields only for
  marketplace pricing/comps.
- Use `append_item_note` for additive private observations on an existing item.
  Do not use `update_item` with `privateNotes` just to append text; existing
  private notes are intentionally not returned by item reads.
- For sell items, create or update a sale listing with listing status,
  platform, title, description, pricing range, research depth, and sources.

For measurements:

- `dimensionsIn.lengthIn` is the long horizontal dimension.
- `dimensionsIn.widthIn` is depth.
- `dimensionsIn.heightIn` is height.
- Use `measurementProvenance` to record source type, confidence, notes,
  recorded time, and whether verification is needed.

## REST API

Base URL:

`https://movingmanifest.com/api/v1`

Auth header:

`Authorization: Bearer mmk_...`

Suggested discovery order:

1. `GET /me`
2. `GET /moves`
3. `GET /moves/{moveId}/agent-context`
4. Read spaces, transport resources, zones, item counts, sale pipeline, and
   existing photos before writing.
5. Store "how transported" as movable-unit assignments. Put newly discovered
   contents, box photos, and linked existing items into one box with
   `save_box_intake`. Capture rough boxes
   and large loose pieces with MCP `batch_upsert_movable_units`, or REST
   `POST /api/v1/moves/{moveId}/movable-units/batch-upsert` when using
   OpenAPI/actions instead of MCP. If a rough row already has a resolved load
   target, include `assignedResourceId` and optional
   `assignedZoneId` on that row; use `apply_assignments` later for stricter
   validation, reassignment, or review-driven load changes. Use item
   `requiresPersonalTransport` or `disposition: "personalTransport"` for
   owner-carried item intent. Treat only true move-as-is loose pieces as
   movable units; ordinary unboxed detailed inventory stays in the unpacked
   queue until it is boxed or deliberately tagged/assigned as a large loose
   unit. Expand numbered box ranges like "boxes 1-25" or
   `B-001-B-025` into one box row per code before calling
   `batch_upsert_movable_units`; each physical box is its own movable unit. If
   the user names a container/material type, set `containerType` on the box row:
   `carton`, `plasticTote`, `bin`, `wardrobe`, `dishPack`, `crate`, or `other`.
   If
   the user gives new code-less boxes such as "12 medium boxes", you may send
   one box row with `count: 12`; the tool expands it and returns
   `unitCountIndex` / `unitCount`. If
   photos are already uploaded for several boxes/totes, put those `photoIds`
   on the matching explicit box rows so the same batch attaches them; do not
   combine `photoIds` with `count`. If
   live box rows have no `boxId` or `code`, pass a stable `idempotencyKey`
   such as `rough-garage-2026-06-19` so retries do not create duplicate
   auto-coded boxes. REST agents use the same `units[]` shape and should send a
   body `idempotencyKey` or `Idempotency-Key` header for live code-less box
   rows. If the tool creates new loose-item rows, include
   `externalSource` plus
   `externalId`; use stable IDs like `garage-treadmill-1` so retries and later
   measurement patches update the same loose unit. New loose rows become
   active, reviewable movable units in the load planner. If the user says a
   loose unit "goes with me",
   "goes in my car", or "do not let movers touch", store that as structured
   owner-carry intent instead of an item note. Preserve response row mapping:
   box results include `unitIndex`, and loose-item batch rows map back with
   `unitIndexes` or `unitIndex`, so created ids, warnings, and row errors can
   be explained against the user's pasted list. Read `movableUnitSummary` from
   `get_agent_context` or `get_move_summary` before asking for measurement
   follow-up; it reports total units, box/loose counts, known weight/volume,
   assignment counts, missing measurement counts, bounded `measurementRoute`
   groups, bounded gap examples, and bounded assignment examples. Use
   `measurementRoute` to suggest the next room/source area to measure, then
   reuse `measurementPatchHint.target` and `assignmentPatchHint.target` from
   grouped or flat examples for follow-up writes instead of guessing IDs or
   creating duplicate units.
   When the user later supplies missing measurements, call
   `batch_upsert_movable_units` again with the existing boxId/code or loose
   itemId and only the new weight, dimensions, volume, or assignment fields.
   Include `photoIds` on box rows when photos need to be attached later.
   Box codes are normalized before matching, so `b 012` and `B-012` target the
   same box.
   Use `get_capacity_report` when checking load fit; resource and zone totals
   include assigned boxes plus assigned large loose items.
6. When opening a rough box later, use `save_box_intake` when named contents,
   box measurements, photos, or linked existing items should be saved into that
   existing box. It returns `boxId`, `boxCode`, `photoIds`, `packedItems`, and a
   verification `nextStep` in `agentReview`; use those IDs in the user summary
   and verify with `get_move_summary` or `get_agent_context` before continuing. If the user queued
   several photos from the scanned/open box, claim that queue with
   `ingestion_queue`, use media `boxId`, queue `targetBoxId`, or queue
   `targetBoxCode` as the target, and submit `committedItems` plus
   `boxAssignments` back into the same box. Do not create a replacement box
   just because the rough box is now being itemized. Tell the user the physical
   follow-up after writing, such as which box code to put on the carton/tote.

Important endpoints:

- `POST /moves`
- `POST /moves/setup`
- `GET /moves/{moveId}/agent-context`
- `GET /moves/{moveId}/items`
- `POST /moves/{moveId}/items`
- `POST /moves/{moveId}/items/batch-upsert`
- `GET /moves/{moveId}/spaces`
- `POST /moves/{moveId}/spaces`
- `POST /moves/{moveId}/sale-listings`
- `POST /photos/upload`
- `POST /images/upload`
- `POST /uploads/init`
- `POST /photos/finalize`
- `GET /moves/{moveId}/capacity-report`
- `GET /moves/{moveId}/move-day`
- `POST /moves/{moveId}/exports`

Use `/openapi.json` for machine-readable endpoint details.

## MCP

MovingManifest exposes one shared MCP server contract through two transports:
a remote endpoint for hosted assistants and a local npx server for desktop/CLI
agents. The published tool surface can differ by auth mode. For first
hosted/mobile OAuth launch, OAuth should use the narrower trusted-helper
surface; local/headless API-key clients can use broader explicitly scoped tools.

Remote MCP (claude.ai custom connectors, Claude Cowork, any Streamable HTTP
client — no install needed):

```
Endpoint: https://movingmanifest.com/api/mcp
Auth:     OAuth via Clerk sign-in/consent, or Authorization: Bearer mmk_replace_with_a_scoped_api_key
```

OAuth-capable clients should connect by endpoint URL and follow the
protected-resource login flow. For the first hosted/mobile OAuth launch,
MovingManifest should set `MOVINGMANIFEST_MCP_OAUTH_TOOLSET=trusted-helper` to
expose only setup, capture queue, researched item, photo, packing, and transport
tools. Scoped `mmk_` keys can still use the broader local/headless tool surface.
Before publish, run the authorized OAuth smoke with
`--expect-trusted-helper-toolset` so the hosted connector proves the narrower
OAuth tool list.
Clients that cannot set custom headers may append `?key=mmk_...` to the endpoint
URL, but header auth is recommended because URLs can be logged.

Local MCP via npx — Codex setup when the user has local shell access:

```bash
codex mcp add movingmanifest \
  --env MOVINGMANIFEST_API_KEY=mmk_replace_with_a_scoped_api_key \
  -- npx -y movingmanifest-mcp
```

Equivalent Codex `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.movingmanifest]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "movingmanifest-mcp"]

[mcp_servers.movingmanifest.env]
MOVINGMANIFEST_API_KEY = "mmk_replace_with_a_scoped_api_key"
```

Claude Desktop and similar JSON-config MCP clients use the same command:
`"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "movingmanifest-mcp"]` with the key in env.

After configuring MCP for Codex, restart Codex or start a fresh session. The
agent should confirm `movingmanifest` appears in `/mcp` or `codex mcp list`,
then call `get_api_context` to verify the current connection before accessing
private data. Check `connection.user.email` and
`connection.householdMember.apiAccessAllowed` when present. If the current Codex
session cannot see newly added MCP tools,
tell the user a fresh Codex session is needed rather than assuming the OAuth
connection, key, or API is broken.

Suggested first MCP tools:

- `agent_workbench`
- `get_api_capabilities`
- `get_api_context`
- `list_moves`
- `get_agent_context`

- `get_api_capabilities`

- `batch_upsert_items`

- `create_item_with_images`
- `upload_photo`
- `upload_photos`

- `ingestion_queue` with `committedItems.appendNote` for trusted queue capture notes and append-safe queue research sources
- `suggest_assignments`

- household member tools such as `list_household_members` and `add_household_member`

## Safety Rules For Assistants

- Ask before using a key if the user has not clearly authorized it.
- Do not store the raw key in generated files.
- Do not expose private values, serials, notes, photos, or addresses in public
  outputs.
- Prefer move-restricted keys when possible.
- Verify writes by reading the created records back.
- Use `agentLabel` and `aiConfidenceScore` on agent-created items, boxes, and
  photos. `aiConfidenceScore` is whole-record confidence from 0 to 1, not a
  measurement confidence field.
- Summarize exactly what changed and what still needs user review.
- Get clear session or batch permission before creating records or uploading
  photos. Once the user has asked the assistant to capture a room, photo, list,
  or batch, do not ask for approval on every ordinary inferred item field.
- Ask explicitly before sensitive actions: marking items for sale, creating
  exports, changing layout/load plans, granting household access, or exposing
  private values, serials, notes, addresses, or photos.
- If dimensions, weight, condition, value, price, or contents are estimated,
  store estimate confidence and provenance instead of presenting guesses as
  facts.
